headline: High: Replit Agent can write and exfiltrate workspace secrets while Authelia exposes broad network/OIDC surfaces, creating default data-leak and compliance risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A direct injection bridge is not documented: Authelia is an auth service with OIDC/ForwardAuth, while Replit Agent operates in a Repl workspace. The only plausible path is manual or file-based handoff, so the blast radius is limited and not default. Uncertainty remains because Replit can read/write workspace files and Authelia can emit auth-related content.
conditions: IF Authelia outputs are copied into Replit workspace files, THEN Replit Agent can treat them as instructions.
IF a shared file or paste bridge is introduced, THEN prompt injection becomes feasible.
mitigations: Keep Authelia outputs out of shared files.
Use a read-only handoff format for any copied text.
Add a human review step before Replit Agent acts on copied content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Replit Agent explicitly touches secrets, source code, and deployment configuration and can read/write the Repl filesystem. Authelia has broad network egress and OIDC/ForwardAuth surfaces, so if its outputs or logs are routed into the Repl workspace, sensitive material can be exposed or forwarded. The pairwise path is plausible in default cloud workflows, so I choose high over medium due to uncertainty.
conditions: IF Authelia logs, tokens, or auth responses are stored in the Repl workspace, THEN Replit Agent can read them.
IF Replit Agent sends workspace contents to external APIs, THEN secrets from the shared workspace can leak.
mitigations: Do not place secrets or auth logs in the Repl workspace.
Rotate any credentials already stored in shared files.
Restrict Replit Agent to a scrubbed test workspace.
Review outbound requests before enabling any integration.
requires-engineering: add secret-redaction and workspace isolation controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Authelia has broad network egress and API-facing auth duties, while Replit Agent can execute shell, modify git state, and write the filesystem in a persistent Repl workspace. That overlap creates a real write-conflict pathway on shared mutable resources if both touch the same repo or deployment config. No locking mechanism is documented, so I treat the conflict as default-possible.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or deployment files, THEN concurrent edits can conflict.
IF Replit Agent commits while Authelia-driven automation also updates the same files, THEN git state can diverge.
mitigations: Assign separate directories or repos.
Pause one agent before the other edits shared files.
Require manual merge review for any git changes.
Use branch-per-agent workflows.
requires-engineering: add file-locking or orchestration locks.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Replit Agent is a full-app builder that can act on workspace content, while Authelia produces authentication-related outputs through OIDC/ForwardAuth. If Authelia-derived text or config is fed into Replit Agent without verification, the agent may implement incorrect auth logic or deployment changes. The pathway is plausible but not directly evidenced, so medium fits better than low.
conditions: IF Authelia-generated config or instructions are passed into Replit Agent, THEN Replit Agent may act on them as authoritative.
IF no human verification step exists, THEN downstream code or deployment changes can propagate errors.
mitigations: Require human review of any auth-related output before action.
Use a checklist for config changes.
Test changes in a throwaway Repl first.
Compare generated config against known-good templates.
requires-engineering: add automated validation for auth and deployment changes.

E_compliance.rationale: Replit Agent explicitly handles secrets and deployment configuration in a cloud Repl, while Authelia is an authentication layer with broad network egress. If regulated credentials or user data are routed through the Repl workspace, retention and residency obligations can diverge from the auth system’s handling. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so I keep this at medium.
conditions: IF regulated secrets or personal data are stored in Replit Secrets or workspace files, THEN Replit retention and access policies apply.
IF Authelia-authenticated user data is copied into the Repl, THEN compliance scope expands to the cloud workspace.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the Repl workspace.
Document which data classes may enter each agent.
Review retention settings for Replit Secrets and files.
Use synthetic data for development.
requires-engineering: perform a formal residency and DPA review.
